findings.claim_text: OpenRouter's provider-selection guide states plainly that its default load-balancer "look[s] at the lowest-cost candidates and select[s] one weighted by inverse square of the price" — literally r=2, spelled out with a worked example ($1 vs. $3 providers split roughly 9-to-1) [^9].
TechCrunch reported on 2026-07-13 — five weeks before the OpenRouter critique — that Robot Ventures was *leading* a new $75 million round valuing Nous Research at $1.5 billion [^35].

A 2026 paper formally proves that splitting one bid across multiple sub-identities in a Tullock procurement contest yields no higher payoff than submitting one consolidated bid [^21], and a survey of the same literature calls Sybil-proofness one of the properties that makes Tullock contests attractive for decentralized infrastructure design in the first place [^20].
